summary: Specifies the Open Shortest Path First routing protocol, an interior gateway protocol that spreads routing information inside one autonomous system. It is based on the link-state approach and not the distance-vector one. It was replaced by RFC 1247.

eli5.summary: Every router learns the whole map and works out the shortest roads for itself, instead of trusting rumors from neighbors.

questions: what are the ospf packet types
subtitle: The first version of OSPF: a link-state routing protocol where every router maps the network and computes its own shortest paths.

tldr.problem: Traditional internet routing protocols were based on Bellman-Ford, and a protocol was needed that responds quickly to topology changes with little routing traffic.
tldr.mechanism: Each router floods its local state, builds an identical topological database for its area, and runs a shortest-path calculation with itself as the root. Areas and a backbone limit how far detailed topology spreads.
tldr.outcome: This RFC specifies OSPF version 1 and was obsoleted by RFC 1247.

today: RFC 1131 is a Proposed Standard that was obsoleted by RFC 1247, so it describes OSPF version 1 only.

sections.title: What OSPF Is
sections.content:
OSPF (Open Shortest Path First) is an Internal Gateway Protocol: it distributes routing information between routers in a single Autonomous System. It is based on SPF, or link-state, technology, a departure from the Bellman-Ford base of traditional internet routing protocols. It was developed by the OSPF working group of the IETF.

The design explicitly supports IP subnetting, TOS-based routing and tagging of externally derived routes. It authenticates routing updates, uses IP multicast, and aims to respond quickly to topology changes with small amounts of routing traffic. OSPF routes by destination IP address and IP Type of Service only, and packets are not encapsulated in extra headers inside the AS.
sections.eli5: Instead of asking neighbors for directions, every router gets a full map of the roads and plans its own best route.

sections.title: The Database and Shortest-Path Tree
sections.content:
Each router keeps a database describing the AS topology as a directed graph. Its vertices are routers, transit networks and stub networks. A router distributes its local state by flooding, and the flooding is reliable, so every router in an area ends up with exactly the same database. All routers then run the same algorithm in parallel, each building a tree of shortest paths with itself as root. Externally derived routes appear on the tree as leaves.

OSPF calculates separate routes for each Type of Service and splits traffic equally among equal-cost routes. Cost is a single dimensionless metric. Hosts reached through a router appear as stub networks with mask 0xffffffff. Networks may be point-to-point, broadcast or non-broadcast.
sections.eli5: Everyone shares the same map, and then each router draws its own shortest-route tree starting from itself.

sections.title: Areas, Backbone and Router Roles
sections.content:
An AS can be split into areas. Each area runs a separate copy of the SPF algorithm and has its own database, and its topology is invisible from outside. This reduces routing traffic and protects intra-area routing from bad information injected from elsewhere. Traffic between areas goes through the backbone, which must be contiguous; configured virtual links can restore connectivity.

Routers fall into four overlapping categories: internal routers, area border routers, backbone routers and AS boundary routers. Area border routers run one copy of the algorithm per attached area and summarize each area for the backbone.
sections.eli5: Big cities are split into neighborhoods. People in one neighborhood know their own streets well and use the main road to reach other neighborhoods.

sections.title: Packets and Operation
sections.content:
OSPF runs directly over IP as protocol 89, with no fragmentation of its own, and packets are sent with IP TOS 0. Routers find neighbors with the Hello protocol, which also elects a Designated Router on multi-access networks, then form adjacencies and synchronize databases. Hellos go to the multicast address AllSPFRouters, 224.0.0.5. Every packet starts with a common 24-byte header, which carries the Version (1 for this specification), the Type, the Router ID, the Area ID and an authentication type with a 64-bit authentication field. Authentication types defined are 0 (none) and 1 (simple password).

There are five packet types: Hello, Database Description, Link State Request, Link State Update and Link State Ack. Link state advertisements are router links, network links, summary links and AS external links, each starting with a 20-byte header. A few architectural constants are fixed: LSRefreshTime is 30 minutes, MinLSInterval is 5 seconds and MaxAge is 1 hour.
sections.eli5: Routers say hello to find neighbors, trade their maps, and send small acknowledgments so nothing gets lost on the way.
